technology transfer to PSUs is important. The Committee would like the Ministry of Health and
Family Welfare to fast track the production of SIPV by PSU and fix a definite time line for the
same. (Para 3.25)
Committee's attention has also been drawn to the recent emergence of type 2 strain of Polio
virus in Uttar Pradesh. This contamination of polio vaccines raises the fear of bringing back type
2 strain of polio virus which was believed to have been eradicated. Such incidents clearly highlight
a huge gap in the vaccine monitoring mechanism and its inefficient quality control measure.
(Para 3.26)
The Committee emphasizes the need to have a robust control over vaccine manufacturing
and recommends strengthening of regulatory mechanism so that such incidents threatening
public health do not occur again and the polio free status of country is not jeopardized. The
Committee also recommends for taking steps to manufacture bulk vaccines within the country.
(Para 3.27)
The Committee is happy to note that the funds allocated for RNTCP for 2017-18 has been
utilized optimally. However, as per the latest WHO's 2018 Global TB Report, the disease burden
caused by TB is falling globally, but to end TB by 2030 countries will have to double their efforts.
Though India leads the world in the burden of tuberculosis, under-reporting and under-diagnosis
of TB cases is a major issue. The Committee urges the Ministry to put in accelerated efforts to
reduce the gap in tuberculosis diagnosis and treatment and improve early detection of tuberculosis.
(Para 3.30)
The Committee would like to draw the attention to the recent Report published in the
Lancet which states that India is unlikely to meet the United Nation's Sustainable Development
Goals (SDG) for 2030 to reduce premature deaths due to major non-communicable diseases
(NCDs). The Lancet reports that in 2016, for people between the age of 30 and 70 in India, the
risk of dying from one of the four major NCDs was 20 per cent in women and 27 per cent in
men. The Committee is dismayed at the increasing burden of Non Communicable diseases in the
country as the statistics suggest that the country has made limited national progress on the
NCDs front. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should take effective
measures to reduce the major risk factors of NCDs and promote lifestyle changes. Early detection
and screening of NCDs are crucial for containing Non Communicable Diseases. (Para 3.33)

project on 5th July, 2016 and Joint Security Review Committee approved in-principle the
construction till 10th floor in March 2018 and above all the Monitoring Cell is being now

64
constituted for monitoring of the project for its completion on time. The Committee, therefore,
apprehends the time and cost overruns. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendation
made in para 3.4 of 106th Report of the Committee. (Para 3.37)
The Committee observes that no new development has taken so far w.r.t the rehabilitation
of jhuggi dwellers and that will result in the delay of the construction of the Modern Maternal
Care Centre in NCT of Delhi. The Committee has not been informed whether the Department
received any response from the DUSIB for the eviction and re-settlement of jhugi dwellers on
priority basis as there is no progress since June, 2017 despite payment of compensatory amount.
The Committee, therefore, urges upon the Department to pursue the matter rigorously with
DUSIB so that the work of construction of modern maternal care centre is started as early as
possible. (Para 3.40)
The Committee observes that 956 posts in the different Departments of the hospital are still
lying vacant which would have an adverse effect on the efficiency and the smooth functioning
of the hospital. The Committee also observes that large number of seats are filled up on contract
basis that is obviously not the long term solution. The Committee, therefore, recommends that
the Department must accelerate the administrative process to fill up the vacant post on regular
basis within a specified period of time. (Para 3.43)
IV. PRADHAN MANTRI SWASTHYA SURAKSHA YOJANA (PMSSY)
Since the budgetary allocation to PMSSY was reduced to ````` 3825.50 Crore in BE 2018-19
against the projected demand of ````` 8398.00 Crore and 4% lesser than BE 2017-18 i.e. to the tune
of ````` 3975.00 Crore on the plea of earmarking additional requirement of fund at RE 2018-19 and
if necessary also form new stream of financial i.e. HEFA for utilization in infrastructural and
research projects under PMSSY, the Committee would like to be apprised of budgetary allocation
at RE 2018-19 and allocation of additional requirement of fund from HEFA along with utilization
of total sum amount on various activities under PMSSY. (Para 3.46)
The Committee is not convinced with the reply given by the Department regarding the lower
allocation of budget and deficiencies related to infrastructure and shortage of faculty & equipments
in the AIIMS like institutions. The Committee apprehends the completion of infrastructural
projects under PMSSY in time with lower budgetary allocation and dependence for additional
requirement to finance such projects from HEFA which is a long drawn source of financing. The
Committee, moreover, observes that infrastructural projects under  phase-I of PMSSY are yet be
completed and the Government has rolled out phase-II, III, IV and V phases of PMSSY without
commensurating allocation of requisite fund. This is mere poor planning with unrealistic objectives
and goal, leaving the progress of execution of on-going project in lurch. The Committee is
surprised to note that the work for Super Speciality Block at Kolkata Medical College was
awarded in February, 2011 but has not been able to complete due to various reasons. The
Committee is anguished over the project status and therefore, strongly recommends the
Department to take immediate steps to resolve the issues and complete the work of Super
Specialty Block within the stipulated time period. (Para 3.55)

65
The Committee takes note of the delay in majority of the projects due to the failure of the
construction contractors, environmental clearance, heavy rainfall etc. The Committee, thus,
reiterates its recommendation to award better and reputed professional agencies like NBCC and
L&T for the timely completion of the projects. The Committee hopes that greater delegation and
empowerment of the procurement support agency system of assigning the construction work to
executing agencies on turnkey basis; online dashboard for effective monitoring; incorporation of
punitive clause in contract conditions and expand means of NBCC for award of new AIIMS work
would incentivize the speedy execution of projects under PMSSY. (Para 3.56)
The Committee is not convinced with the reply given by the Department w.r.t. financing of
the projects by the Ministry through different financing agencies. The Committee therefore,
reiterates its view that financing of the projects through these external agencies would be a long
drawn process and since PMSSY is an ambitious scheme to improve the condition of the Health
Sector in the country, any inordinate delay in the generation and allocation of the funds through
external agencies will hamper the scheme. The Committee would like to reiterate that the
Department should devise a prudent fiscal and feasible fiscal policy for generating and allocating
financial resources for allocation of committed funds for the PMSSY scheme. The Committee
also recommends the Department to take up the matter on priority basis and devise a suitable
roadmap for the generation of the funds from both sources i.e., internal and external. The
Committee, however, would like to be apprised of the details of the amount funded by the Japan
International Cooperation Agency and from HEFA, the time frame by when these funds would
be made available for utilization under PMSSY. (Para 3.59)
The Committee underscores the efforts of the Government in promoting Make-in-India
programme and feels that all Department /Ministries would prioritize their programmes/schemes
in a manner, so as to give impetus to the cherished mission of Make-in-India programme. The
Committee, in this regard, recommends that the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare would also
contribute by encouraging the procurement of equipments with BIS specification. The Committee,
therefore, recommends to the Department to take up the matter with BIS to issue guidelines
with all specification of international standard and practices pertaining to all medical devices and
make it mandatory for procurement of all medical equipment with BIS Certification/authentication.
(Para 3.63)
The Committee observes with concern that out of sanctioned faculty of 1830 posts, only 808
posts have been filled up till 21st March, 2018. From the information submitted by the Department
w.r.t to the vacancy at the 6 AIIMS, the Committee gathers that the current situation of the
faculty strength at the 6 AIIMS is abysmal and the same will not only adversely affect the
functioning of the institutions but also the service provided by the institutions to the public. The
Committee understands that the chain impact of deficiency or absence of one category of health
personnel is not restricted to "a particular service" delivery but impacts the whole chain of
integrated nature of functioning of a modern hospital. Moreover, deficiency of personnel means
overburdening of the personnel at work who in turn have to work under intense pressure of
working environment with lop-sided Doctor: patient ratio. Such uneven and peculiar working
equilibrium adversely affect the professional pursuits and morale of the health personnel in

66
these institutions of national importance. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendations
to take up issue of shortage of the manpower in these tertiary care sectors on priority basis and
complete the recruitment process within the stipulated time. (para 3.69)
The Committee has been given to understand that the State Government of Nagaland has
signed an MoU clearly agreeing that the excess cost and recurring expenses of new medical
college at Kohima will be met by the State Government. The Committee furthers notes that
approved cost is being shared between center and the state in the ratio 90:10 and there is no
provision of releasing of excess central share. The Committee is of the view that Central
Government plays a stewardship role, and has a key planning and oversight role, with a consolidated
national information infrastructure necessary to adequately monitor health outcomes, while the
states are responsible for the implementation of programmes. However, a realistic assessment
of the cost estimates in constructing/upgrading a medical college needs to be done so as to make
it possible to operantionalize the medical college with the given funds. The Committee, also notes
that Department has released ````` 165.10 crore till date but physical progress made in establishing
the medical college has not been furnished to the Committee for its consideration. The Committee,
therefore, recommends the Department to reassess the funds actually required for establishing
a medical college that roughly works out to be ````` 400.00 Crore. Further, given the development
status of North-east region, all out efforts must be made to improve the health facilities as well
as provision of health institutions with adequate infrastructure and research activities to take
care of suffering patients. (Para 3.72)
The Committee expresses its deep anguish that State Government of Nagaland has not
submitted utilization Certificate nor reported physical progress on the online monitoring dashboard
despite release of amount to the tune of `````76.03 crore of the Central Share of total amount of
`````170.10 crore out of the approved cost grant of `````189.00 crore on 29th December, 2014 for
upgradation of District Naga hospital, Kohima under the centrally sponsored scheme for
"Establishment of new medical colleges attached with existing District/Referral Hospital" on
Centre and State sharing ratio of 90:10. That is so, despite signing of a MoU by the State
Government of Nagaland that excess cost and recurring expenses of New Medical College at
Kohima would be met by the State Government. Keeping in view the administrative statements
between Central government and State Government of Nagaland the Committee recommends for
higher level of executive intervention to resolve the issue making plea that establishing a
medical college would cater to the healthcare needs of local population. Alternatively, Naga
Hospital at Kohima, Nagaland may be brought under PMSSY and declared as AIIMS like Institution
and accordingly, budgetary allocation be earmarked for the purpose as the same would remove
the financial resource constraints of State Government of Nagaland besides overcoming the
challenge of ensuring public healthcare facility for all in the State and the population around.
(Para 3.76)
V. CENTRAL GOVERNMENT HEALTH SCHEME (CGHS)
Despite the various efforts undertaken by the Department for attracting GDMOs and Non-
Teaching Specialists to join CGHS Wellness centre, shortage of doctors persists. Out of 1848

67
sanctioned posts of allopathic doctors, 436 posts are lying still vacant. The Committee is of the
view that the Department, apart from the steps taken, may consider to give higher remuneration
and attractive incentives for inducting qualified doctors and health personnel to CGHS Wellness
Centre so that CGHS is able to provide efficient and quality health care facilities to its beneficiaries
to more than 32.12 lakh and serving more than 10 lakh cardholders. (Para 3.79)
The Committee expresses its extreme displeasure that the Department has maintained stoic
silence on the issues of the harassment faced by cancer patients who are senior citizens/pensioners
in getting proper treatment in CGHS empanelled hospitals and the simplification of paper work/
procedure involved in the treatment of the cancer patients. The Committee, therefore, reiterates
its recommendations for the simplification of paperwork. The Committee notes that there are
no different referral protocols for critically ill patients including cancer patients. CMO can issue
permission for follow up treatment for period upto six months and there is also provision for
cancer treatment from non-empanelled hospitals at CGHS rates. However, how far this policy has
been implemented is not known to the Committee. The Committee desires that feedback from
patients especially critically ill patients, patients who are senior citizens etc. who encounter
routine problems in getting treatment, admission in hospitals etc., need to be collected out so
that CGHS beneficiaries especially senior citizens do not run from pillar to post for treatment.
The Committee further recommends to the Ministry to issue advisory to all the empanelled
hospitals to be sensitive towards critically ill patients and to be made aware of circulars regarding
simplification of procedures. (Para 3.82)
VI. ALL INDIA INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCES (AIIMS), DELHI
The Committee observes that there is delay in almost all the projects of AIIMS, Delhi. It
speaks volumes of lack of seriousness on the part of the Ministry in getting the work done in
time. The Committee would like to emphasize that health infrastructure is an important indicator
for understanding the health care policy and welfare mechanism in a country. It signifies the
budgetary allocation priority with regards to the creation of health care facilities. The delay in
the projects would have an adverse effect on the services provided by the institutions and would
also increase the expenditure on these projects, the Committee apprehend. The Committee,
thus, recommends the Department to sensitize the implementing agencies to complete the
undertaken projects on priority basis by formulating strategies to complete the projects in a time
bound manner and the Department should make the authorities concerned accountable to ensure
accomplishment of the physical and financial targets of the projects within the set time and cost
limits. (Para 3.86)
The Committee would like to be apprised of the progress made in the process of recruitment
of 150 faculty members that has been advertised on 8th June, 2018. The Committee also desires
a status note on vacant posts, faculty and non-teaching, nursing and support services, technical
and non-technical in various Departments at AIIMS and steps taken/being taken/can further be
taken up to fill-up those vacant posts. (Para 3.89)
VII. REGIONAL INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCES (RIMS), IMPHAL
The Committee observes that against the projected demand of ````` 558.81 Crore a sum of
````` 201.40 Crore has been allocated in BE 2018-19 to RIMS, Imphal. The figure of ````` 201.40 crore

68
is against the projected demand of ````` 558.81 crore under BE. It may be very difficult for RIMS
to come out of the cycle of being allocated a lesser amount in BE stage and then increased to
RE stage, and then subsequently lowered down to a lower amount in the immediately succeeding
BE. The Committee recommends that RIMS may be treated as an equally important Institution
having over 1000 beds for budgetary allocation. The Committee also noted that HSCC (I) Ltd.
rendered the works the fifth time on 24th April, 2018 under Phase-II Project (balance work of
4 hostels and new OPD Block to increase MBBS seats from 100 to 154, largely due to unwillingness
of agencies from outside the state and non fulfillment of the eligibility criteria for local contractors
as mentioned in NIT. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends for a review of eligibility
criteria and explores the possibility of relaxing the same enabling the local contractors to participate
in the bidding/tender process so that the undertaken projects do not suffer further.
(Para 3.94)
The Committee observes that the budgetary allocation of `````309.83 crore to the RIMS for the
year 2017-18 was not sufficient to meet the infrastructural requirements of the Institute and still
the BE for the year 2018-19 has been reduced to Rs 201.40 crore. The Committee, thus, strongly
recommends to the Department to enhance the budgetary allocation at the revised estimates
stage so that the infrastructural problem does not act as a constraint for the Faculty/doctors in
providing their services to the public. (Para 3.97)
The Committee, keeping in view the need for strengthening the healthcare facilities in NER,
recommends for higher budgetary allocation at BE 2018-19 to RIMS commensurating to funds
requirement for starting super-specialty hospital/DM/McH Course and creation for faculty post
and super specialty posts and proposal for construction of super specialty block. The Committee
further recommends that RIMS, Imphal assess the fund requirement of proposed projects,
prepare DPR and submit the same for approval of Competent Authority and forward the projected
demand to the Ministry of Finance for its kind perusal and consideration. The Ministry of Health
and Family Welfare must co-ordinate in- tendem with RIMS and the Ministry of Finance and
other competent authority concerned for approval of the projects. (Para 3.100)
VIII. NORTH-EASTERN INDIRA GANDHI REGIONAL INSTITUTE OF HEALTH AND MEDICAL
SCIENCES (NEIGRIHMS), SHILLONG
The Committee is perturbed to note that as against the allocation of ````` 335 crore during the
years 2017-18, the Department has utilized only ````` 259.49 crore till 31.3.2018 which is only 77 %
of the total allocated funds. The underutilization of the funds will result in delay of the completion
of the project that would, in turn, increase the overall cost of construction. The Committee, thus,
reiterates its recommendation to make the prudent assessment of the allocation of the funds to
avoid the problem of underutilization of the funds. The Committee would like to be apprised of
the time frame within which the construction of the Medical College building and expansion of
the Medical College at the NEIGRIHMS would be completed. The Committee also reiterates its
recommendation for optimum utilization of available infrastructure at NEIGRIHMS and developing
functional synergy amongst various healthcare institutes in NER so as to facilitate the patients
with utmost healthcare and comfort level. (Para 3.104)

69
IX. NATIONAL AIDS CONTROL ORGANIZATION (NACO)
The Committee is anguished to find the actual expenditure booked by NACO during
2017-18 was to the tune of ````` 2001.50 Crore against the provision of ````` 2163 Crore, thus with an
overall savings of ````` 153.26 Crore on various scheme/programme on account of various reasons
viz. non-abortive capacity, non-materialization of certain item of procurement, non-fulfillment of
mandatory requirement of release under GFR. The Committee finds this state of affairs as
undesirable and therefore, strongly recommends the Department to pull up the implementing
agencies for optimum utilization of allocated fund for the intended purpose by enhancing the
absorption-capacity of the scheme programme so that the case/justification for budgetary allocation
as per projected demand in upcoming financial years would yield positive response from the
Ministry of Finance.
(Para 3.107)
METRO BLOOD BANKS
The Committee wonders at the response of the Department to the Committee's
recommendations that entails certain course of action on the part of the Department but the
Department mention in its action taken note that the observation has been noted for compliance,
that too without furnishing information on the progress of project, the setting up of Metro Blood
Banks at Chennai and Kolkata in the instant case. (Para 3.110)
The Committee observes that approval for establishing only two Metro Blood Banks at
Chennai and Kolkata in the country since the inception of the project has been given. The
Committee is of the considered view that project for setting up Metro Blood Bank, a state-of-
the-art facility that will serve as a central point for processing of blood components and their
supply besides coordinating with other health centres, should not have been delayed. The Committee
would like to be apprised with reasons for the year's long delay in getting the approval for the
setting up of Metro Blood banks at two places. The status of other two sites, Delhi and Mumbai
has also not been provided. The Committee would like to be apprised of the progress made in
acquisition of land in respect of remaining of two Blood Banks. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Department should devise an action plan and fix the timeline for the
completion of the projects. The Committee also desires that the process of allocation and utilization
of funds and necessary approvals for operationalization of the approved projects should be
expedited. (Para 3.111)
IV. DR. RAM MANOHAR LOHIA (RML) HOSPITAL, NEW DELHI AND PGIMER, DR. RML
HOSPITAL, NEW DELHI
The Committee would like to be apprised of the progress made in completion of infrastructure
project to endow the RML Hospital with the modern healthcare facilities which inter-alia include
Committee of a forensic medicine department, creation of 1051 new posts of different categories,
three OT in New ECS Building, 15 bedded ICU on 1st Floor, Super Speciality OPD consisting of
10 rooms; expansion of OPD area; conversion of cafeteria of PGIMER into Seminar; shifting of
NUT; upgradation and renovation of all the 16 OTs; procurement of 5 High Technology Patient
Transport Ambulance; project on para medical college and re-constructing of Nursing College.
(Para 4.3)

Recommendation

Further Recommendation

its requirements of funds at the stage of Revised Estimate for 2018-19 to complete the

be apprised of the funds received at RE stage and the physical achievement of ongoing/

would also hold budget discussion  2019-20 with Ministry of Finance and effectively place  its

under-utilization of funds with respect to certain schemes/projects like Development of Tools to
prevent Outbreaks of epidemics (33.20%); Human Resource Development for Health Research

prepare Comprehensive Action Plan for the purpose spelling the fund requirement and time
frame work.
VI. DEVELOPMENT OF TOOLS/SUPPORT TO PREVENT OUTBREAKS OF EPIDEMIC
Recommendation
3.45 The Committee has been given to understand that the inadequacy of specialized laboratories
equipped with latest equipment in the country, especially at secondary and tertiary level has
severely affected the response time in identification of the viruses and quick mobilization in the
event of out-breaks/ r esponse to infectious disease out-breaks/epidemics, viz, the H1N1 viruses
that gripped the nation in 2010 and during the Swine flu outbreaks in the past. The Committee,
however, finds that a budget line created in 2015-16 is being allocated meagre amount of 
` 5.00
crore in RE 2017-18 to meet expenditure for supply of diagnostic kits, transport of samples, hiring
of additional manpower , etc. during such outbreak. The Committee notes that during the year 2017-18,
the Department has utilised 80% of the allocation upto 31st January, 2018. The Committee also
takes into account details of action plan for the year 2018-19 encompassing various activities. In
view of this, the Committee recommends that the Department should take up with the Ministry of
Finance for higher allocation at RE stage. (Para 6.4)
Action Taken
3.46 The utilization under this component in 2017-18 was ` 4.97 crores against the RE allocation

14
of `5.00 crores (99.4%). BE 2018-19 is `5.00 crores and additional requirements, if any, would
be projected at the RE stage, based on the progress of expenditure and demands from the State
Governments/Medical Colleges/Research Institutes, etc.
Further Recommendation
3.47 The Committee is of the considered view that adequate number of specialised laboratories
equipped with latest tools support system and adequate skilled manpower at secondary and
tertiary level  is required to reduce  the response  time in identification of  the viruses to
control, contain and eliminate the viral agents in the event of outbreaks of new viral
agents. The Committee, therefore, recommends that adequate funds must be earmarked for
development of tools/support system for preparedness of early diagnosis of viral epidemics.
The Committee points out that DHR must have placed projected the additional fund requirements
at RE Stage in 2018-19. It hopes that the Ministry of Finance would allocate adequate fund
as per requirement in the financial year 2019-20.
VII NORTH EASTERN AREAS
Recommendation
3.48 The Committee observes that the initiatives have been taken by the Department to undertake
studies and projects specific to North-eastern region and exhorts that focussed attention  be paid
to be the implementation of the undertaken projects by  way of streamlined monitoring so that
tangible outcomes so achieved and benefits emerging, there from could percolate down to the
common people, especially downtrodden and low income group people. (Para 7.4)
Action Taken
3.49 ICMR has a permanent Institute at Dibrugarh and addressing various health issues of the
regional importance. Also Three Task Force projects have been initiated recently in north east by
ICMR as mentioned below:
 Rickettsial diseases in states of Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram in Northeast India:
Epidemiology, disease burden and vectors.
 Systematic study of Acute Encephalitis Syndrome (AES) in NE states of India for
clinical, aetiological and epidemiological aspects.
 Monitoring of insecticide resistance  in malaria vectors in endemic States of India
(VBDSF) including North East Region.
3.50 Similarly, the research projects funded by the Department of Health Research under its
schemes are based on national health priorities as well as regional/local health issues and are
intended to achieve tangible outcomes for the benefit of public at large, particularly the downtrodden
and low income and tribal population, etc.
Further Recommendation
3.51 The Committee believes that Regional Medical Research Centre, Dibrugarh is promoting
various research field stations in region in accomplishing the objectives of extramural projects
and the outcome of all such research activities benefits the common people with special

15
emphasis on low income group and down trodden  people  while combating the life threatening
diseases. The Committee also hopes that the Bio-medical Research Centre would be established
in Guwahati without time and cost overruns. The Committee further hopes that DHR would
achieve the target of setting up of MRUs and MRHRUs in NER and utilise the fund of `````3.00
crore meant  for Human Resource Development for health Research in these Sates during
the year 2018-19.  The Committee further recommend for provision of adequate fund during
the year 2019-20  under this head for accomplishing the set objective during that financial
year.
Recommendation
3.52 The Committee observes the financial performance under North-East component during 2016-17
and 2017-18. The Committee observes that against the allocation of 
` 75.00 crore during 2016-17,
the actual expenditure remained to the tune of ` 57.17 crore, thus leaving an unspent amount to
the tune of `17.83 crore which is a matter of concern to the Committee. The Committee notes
components of various schemes to be undertaken during 2018-19 and expects that there would be
optimal utilization of allocated funds on various projects. (Para 7.5)
Action Taken
3.53 The Schemes viz. Programmes of Department of Health Research are mostly Government
Medical College centric. Out of 7 NE States, 4 NE States – Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Nagaland
and Sikkim have no Government Medical College. ICMR has only one Institute in NE region,
namely the Regional Medical Research Centre (RMRC), Dibrugarh. As a part of the efforts to
improve the expenditure profile on health research activities in the NE region, it has been decided
to establish a Bio Medical Research Centre at Guwahati. All effort will be made by Department of
Health Research and ICMR to enhance the research activities by way of funding more research
projects in the NE region to ensure optimum utilization of the allocation under NE component.
Further Recommendation
3.54 The Committee expresses its displeasure that there is no Government Medical College
in Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Nagaland and Sikkim.  However, the Committee is aware
that setting up Government Medical Colleges is in the domain of the Department of Health
and Family Welfare. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the Department
of Health Research should take up the issue to set up Government Medical Colleges cum
Hospital in all the  four  States without further delay to ensure that these four States are
not bereft of medical services available to other parts of the country.

The Committee believes that the Department of Health Research had effectively forwarded
its requirements of funds at the stage of Revised Estimate for 2018-19 to complete the

be apprised of the funds received at RE stage and the physical achievement of ongoing/
already sanctioned projects against the set targets. The Committee also believes that DHR
would also hold budget discussion  2019-20 with Ministry of Finance and effectively place  its
projected demand as per Comprehensive Action Plan, as noted by DHR in Para 2.3 of  107th
Report for compliance. In this regard, the Committee would like to be apprised of the
ingredients of Comprehensive Action Plan of DHR and the requirement of funds to accomplish
the set objectives/targets. (Para 3.3)
The Committee notes the measures taken by DHR to ensure the optimum utilisation
of allocated funds on various schemes, although adequate appropriation of funds at BE
Stage, itself would ensure execution of schemes as per originally conceived time frame and
not at the fag end/ last quarter of financial year. That would also ensure compliance of
guideline of the Ministry of Finance as regards streamlining  and even further expenditure
throughout the financial year. (Para 3.7)
The Committee would like to be apprised of the outcome of the measures taken for
financial integration between DHR and ICMR and the outcome of the efforts so undertaken
for better/efficient management and implementation of the scheme/program mes. (Para 3.8)
The Committee would like to be apprised of the projected demands of DHR at stage
2018-19 and the actual allocation made against each scheme. The Committee further  believes
that web-based portal for better monitoring mechanism would yield in efficient  and effective
execution of undertaken schemes/projects. (Para 3.11)
III INDIAN COUNCIL OF MEDICAL RESEARCH (ICMR)
The Committee appreciates that ICMR has been entrusted  with the pivotal task of
formulating conducting and promoting biomedical research with cherished objective of National
Health priorities covering control and management of communicable diseases, fertility control,
maternal and child health, control of nutrational disorders, challenges of environmental and
occupational health problems, conducting  research on non-communicable diseases as well.
The Committee, therefore, desires that the DHR apprise the Committee about the projected
demand of DHR at RE Stage and the actual allocation of fund at RE 2018-19.  The Committee
further believes that DHR would hold effective brain storming  session to assess the actual
requirement of fund for various ongoing/pending and new schemes to be launched  during
2019-20 and accordingly project its demand in BE 2019-20 with due diligence and proper
justification. The Committee would urge Ministry of Finance to consider provision of adequate
fund as component of its fundamental priorities. (Para 3.14)
The Committee desires the DHR to apprise it whether the Ministry of Finance has
allocated the Department  and additional funds to the tune of `````350.00 crore for 2018-19 at

18
RE Stage for execution of ongoing schemes as undertaken by ICMR, and ensure that all
research activities are implemented as per set time frames. The Committee also strongly
recommends that Ministry of Finance may consider to allocate adequate fund to ICMR in
the financial year  2019-20 so that research activities of  ICMR do not suffer for want of
fund as outcome of health related research activities would save millions of lives in the
country. (Para 3.17)
During the course of examination of Demands for Grants (2018-19), the DHR had
submitted that “against the projected  demand of `````2487.00 crore for the year 2018-19 an
allocation of ````` 1416.00 crore was made to the ICMR with the shortfall of `````1071.00 crore.
On being enquired about the shortfall,  the Department has clarified that atleast `````350.00
crore is required to cater ongoing research activities. Out of this ````` 200.00 crore is required
for  ongoing activities and programs (India TB Research Consortium, Malaria Elimination,
INDIAB study, Hypertension study, Human Resource Development and capacity building
programs, Infrastructure Development projects) and ````` 150.00 core for proposed /future
activities and programs (projects related to National Nutrition  Mission, ICMR Academy,
Indo-Africa Initiative, Big Data Analytics, large scale surveys. Mission Mode Projects and
Centres of Excellence, Infrastructure Development Projects. (Para 3.20)
The Committee, in this connection, recommends  that DHR may persuade the Ministry
of Finance to allocate the fund in Financial year 2019-20 as per actual requirement for
research ongoing/new activities during 2019-20. (Para 3.21)
The Committee is of the considered view that ICMR must not face the financial
constraints while implementing its schemes on the intramural and extramural research
activities. The Committee underscore the important impact of projects of ICMR on Bio-
medical research and  developing new drugs, vaccine and diagnostics Kitts in salvaging the
suffering  huge number of mankind from scourge of diseases. The Committee, therefore
recommends the Ministry of Finance to be considerated to the funds  requirement on these
projects. The Committee would like DHR to apprise how much fund was allocated  for
accomplishing these projects during  2018-19 and the fund requirement  for these projects
during 2019-20. (Para 3.24)
The Committee expects that Evidence to Policy (E2P) and communication unit of ICMR
would translate all ICMR research activities into Policy formulation to ensure that the
benefits of the bio-medical health research activities are better communicated to all medical
practitioners at the ground level and life threatening diseases could be combated. It is
therefore important that commercialisation and popularisation of health research activities/
technologies of ICMR must get due attention. (Para 3.27)
The Committee app reciates the initiatives of ICMR towards combating malnutrition
and also the impact assessment  studies on Mid-Day-Meal  programme nutrition, Intervention
in adolescent girls in Navodaya Schools, ‘Establishment of Nutrition Smart Village and
Backyard Nutrigardens’. However, the prevailing deficiency in calorie intake is a grave
form of malnutrition, especially in less developed states of the country like Jharkhand,
Odisha, MP, Bihar, Rajasthan and more tragically even in Delhi in recent times. ICMR

19
needs to reorient its strategy to combat malnutrition in villages and tribal areas. The
Committee hopes that ICMR would make sincere efforts in the light of studies on
malnutrition. (Para 3.30)
The Committee, therefore strongly recommends that ICMR should in consultation with
all Ministries/Department concerned scale up this programme to ensure that enough data
is generated to enable the Government to formulate policies on malnutrition for poorer
section of society especially in villages and tribal areas. (Para 3.31)

II. BUDGET ALLOCATION
Recommendation
1.1  The Committee is constrained to note that despite the projected requirement of 
` 2797.96 crore for
2018-19, the Ministry of AYUSH has been allocated ` 1626.37 crore leaving a shortfall of ` 1171.59 crores.
The Committee also takes note of the meager increase in allocation for central sector and centrally sponsored
schemes from 2017-18 to 2018-19. The Committee, time and again, has been recommending for increasing
the budgetary allocation for the Ministry keeping in view the scope and reach of AYUSH in the life of the
people. Given the popularity, cost effectiveness and as an alternative to modern system of medicine i.e.
Allopathy, the Ministry of AYUSH through its various schemes/ programmes/ vision can help people through
its various remedies/ cure and emerge as a solid system of medicine in healthcare delivery. Accordingly, the
Committee is of the considered view that there needs to be a quantum jump in the budgetary allocation of the
Ministry of AYUSH so that the very objectives of the Ministry to position AYUSH systems as the preferred
system of living and practice for attaining a healthy India is realized. However, in view of the shortfall of
funds for 2018-19, the Committee recommends to the Ministry to judiciously utilize the allocated funds and
deploy the available resources in an efficient manner. (Para 2.4)
Action Taken
1.2 The Ministry agrees with the view of the Committee that there is a need for a quantum jump in the
budgetary allocations so that it can contribute more effectively for attaining a healthy India. To this end, the
Ministry will make every effort to obtain additional funds at RE stage. Further, the recommendation of the
Committee to judiciously utilize the available resources has been taken note and steps will be taken to
regularly monitor the pace of utilization of funds so that remedial action can be taken, if required.
Recommendation
1.3 The Committee is anguished to see the meager allocation given to Ministry of AYUSH compared to
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. Since the year 2013-14, allocation for the Ministry of AYUSH is
between 3% to 4% of the Health Budget. It is 3.08% of the Health Budget for the year 2018-19. The
Committee would like to emphasize that the Department of AYUSH was granted the status of Ministry on
9th November, 2014 as it envisaged development and implementation of programmes and policy formulation
for the growth, development and propagation of AYUSH systems of Healthcare. In view of the fact that
the Ministry is being given a miniscule budgetary allocation compared to Ministry of Health and Family
Welfare, the Committee believes that the Ministry of AYUSH would not be able to realize its objectives
and tap the full potential of the AYUSH systems. The Committee would like to reiterate that adequate
funding is essential for proper development of the AYUSH systems of medicine which has the capacity to
emerge as an alternative system of medicine through quality research, quality AYUSH services,
standardization of AYUSH drugs etc. The Committee, accordingly, recommends that given the vital
importance of the AYUSH systems, atleast 5% of the total Health Budget should be allocated for Ministry
of AYUSH mandatorily to boost up this sector. The Committee therefore recommends that the Ministry of
AYUSH should chalk out a solid fiscal roadmap for optimal utilisation of budgeted funds and thereafter
2

3
take up with the Ministry of Finance the issue of earmarking atleast 5% of the total Health Budget for
Ministry of AYUSH on priority basis. In the same vein, the Committee would recommend that the Ministry
should exercise due diligence in its budget formulation, so that ambitious budgeting is commensurate with
its ability or capacity to absorb the enhanced funds and scarce resources deployable elsewhere do not
remain idly parked. (Para 2.6)
Action Taken
1.4 The Ministry proposes to convey to the Ministry of Finance the strong reservations of the Committee
over the inadequate allocation of funds for AYUSH and in particular to raise the allocation to at least 5 per
cent of the total Health Budget towards Ministry of AYUSH on priority basis.  As advised by the Committee,
the Ministry will exercise due diligence in budget formulation and for its optimal deployment.
III. QUALITY  CONTROL  OF  AYURVEDA,  SIDDHA,  UNANI  AND  HOMOEOPATHIC  (AYUSH)
DRUGS
Recommendation
1.5 The Committee appreciates the efforts made by the Ministry of AYUSH for monitoring of AYUSH
advertisements. Due to the monitoring by Advertising Standards Council of India (ASCI) and the Grievances
against Misleading Advertisements (GAMA), 65% of the advertisements found misleading were withdrawn
or rectified and the rest forwarded to State AYUSH Drug Regulators. The Committee is of the view that
collaborative efforts of the Ministry along with Department of Consumer Affairs, Ministry of Information
& Broadcasting and State Governments have certainly given results as misleading advertisements with
respect to ASU&H drugs which have been unregulated so far have been controlled to an extent. The Committee
feels that it is the need of the hour to strictly monitor and regulate the misleading advertisements for
promoting the sale of AYUSH medicine. Hence, the role of the Ministry of AYUSH is pivotal in proactively
pursuing the issue with other Departments/ Ministries/ ASCI on a regular basis for effectively preventing the
publication of inappropriate/misleading advertisements. (Para 3.12)
Action Taken
1.6 Ministry has proactively pursued the matter of controlling the misleading advertisements of AYUSH
with the following steps-
(i) The matter of misleading AYUSH advertisements appearing in print and electronic media has
been taken up with the media regulators like Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology
and Ministry of Information & Broadcasting and their suggestions/comments incorporated in
evolving the provisions of rules for prohibition of such advertisements.  The draft rules thus
framed have been subjected to consultation with the Drugs Controller General (India) and
Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani Drugs Technical Advisory Board (ASUDTAB) for concurrence and
to enable further action.
(ii) Ministry of Information & Broadcasting issued instructions/guidelines dated 12th July, 2017 to
all media channels to advertise only those AYUSH products which have valid manufacturing
license and to abstain from telecasting such misleading advertisements which are in contravention
of the provisions of the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954
and Rules thereunder.

4
(iii) Ne wly implemented Central Scheme of Pharmacovigilance of ASU&H Drugs also has a
component of monitoring of misleading advertisement by the peripheral centres of the
pharmacovigilance network being developed.
(iv) An Empowered Committee of interdepartmental officers has recently been notified with specific
ToRs of periodic review, monitoring and recommendations for necessary remedial measures
to address the issues and complaints of exaggerated claims and inappropriate advertisements
of AYUSH.
(v) Ministry conducted seven regulatory & quality control training programs of AYUSH across the
country from 22 January, 2018 to 17
thMarch, 2018 for the regulators & manufacturers, in
which intense focus was imparted to the trainees/participants about the technical and regulatory
irregularities of AYUSH advertisements and the provisions of Drugs & Magic Remedies
(Objectionable Advertisements) Act and Rules.
(vi) S tates/UTs have been directed to appoint Gazetted Officers for territorial monitoring of AYUSH
advertisements under the provisions of  Drugs & Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements)
Act and to nominate Nodal Officers for dealing with public complaints of misleading AYUSH
advertisements registered in the GAMA (Grievances Against Misleading Advertisements) Portal
maintained by the Department of Consumer Affairs.
(vii) During the period from 20th January, 2017 to 19th January, 2018, about 456 complaints of
misleading AYUSH advertisements are reported to have been escalated to the State regulators
for appropriate action and 233 advertisers complied with the ASCI’s recommendations either
by modifying or withdrawing the advertisements.

CHAPTER  II
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE TO
PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLIES
II. BUDGET ALLOCATION
Recommendation
2.1 The Committee has been given to understand that the funds remained unutilised for some schemes
of the Ministry due to non-receipt of suitable project proposals, delay in the construction work and
transfer of money to various institutes for starting extension centres. The Committee perceives the reasons
for under-utilization of funds as procedural hickups which could have been avoided if the Ministry had
proactively pursued the issues concerned and streamlined its monitoring mechanism. The Committee takes
cognizance of the steps taken by the Ministry for optimum utilization of funds but would like to emphasize
that if the Ministry needs more budgetary allocation for proper implementation of its various schemes/
programmes, it should be able to show judicious and full utilization of allocated funds thereby justifying
its demand for additional funds. The Committee, therefore, recommends to the Ministry to closely monitor
the utilization of funds for any  scheme and take corrective measures so as to expedite matters where
chances of procedural delay is anticipated. (Para 2.10)
Action Taken
2.2  Keeping in view  under utilisation of funds in some of the Schemes in the previous years, this Ministry
has taken various steps to minimize the bottlenecks for releasing the funds on account of procedural formalities
which resulted in satisfactory expenditure at the RE stage. Due to the satisfactory utilization of funds, an
additional allocation of  ` 129.15 crore over and above BE 2017-18 was received in RE. The actual utilization of
funds during 2017-18 was much higher than that of the previous years and the actual expenditure was
` 1544.49 crore which is 99.15 per cent of the RE. Further, the allocation for 2018-19 also shows a significant
improvement with an additional allocation of  ` 197.72 crore over BE 2017-18.  This Ministry will put its best
efforts and show the similar resolve to achieve higher utilization of funds in the current Financial Year as well.

CHAPTER III
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF THE
GOVERNMENT HA VE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE
II. BUDGET  ALLOCATION
Recommendation
3.1 The Committee is constrained to note that the issue of pendency of UCs has become a perennial
problem. Despite recommendations of the Committee to liquidate the pending UCs, there are still 1082
pending UCs amounting to 
` 524.56 crores. Out of 1082 pending UCs, 622 pertain to National Medicinal
Plants Board amounting to ` 94.78 crore and 244 pertain to National AYUSH Mission amounting to `
391.34 crore. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends to the Ministry to liquidate the pending UCs
and sort out this issue especially for the two schemes indicating high pendency. The Ministry should make
concerted efforts to operationalize the portal as early as possible for online transmission of UCs. The
Committee also recommends to the Ministry to have a monitoring mechanism in place to check high pendency
of UCs with respect to certain schemes having pending UCs since 2001-02. (Para 2.16)
Action Taken
3.2 The Ministry is fully committed to liquidating for UCs under these two Schemes.  Following new
remedial actions have been taken by the Ministry to reduce the pendency of Utilization Certificates (UCs) in
respect of erstwhile Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Development of AYUSH Hospitals & Dispensaries and
National AYUSH Mission (NAM):
(a) Time to time letters have also been written to States/UTs Government from Secretary (AYUSH),
Joint Secretary and Director regarding liquidation of Utilization Certificates.
(b) Regional level workshops cum review meeting for various States have been conducted at
various States under the Chairmanship of Joint Secretary (AYUSH) regarding pendency of
Utilization Certificates.
(c) Relevant supporting documents with respect to Utilization Certificates from States/UTs are
being received through email and the same are being examined as per the GFR provisions for
early settlement of the UCs.
In respect of NMPB, State-wise Nodal Officers are continuously liaising with the respective State
Authorities to take up the matter of liquidation of pending UCs on priority basis.  In addition, Officers are
also deputed to the States/Institutes periodically for liquidating the pending UCs.
Further Recommendation

liquidation of pending UCs, the issue of high pendency of UCs is not solved.  The Committee is also

earliest so that the matter of pendency of UCs is solved.  The Committee also would like the
Ministry to lay special focus on the two schemes, namely, National Medicinal Plants Board and
National AYUSH Mission where number of pendency of UCs is quite high.

III. QUALITY CONTROL OF AYURVEDA, SIDDHA, UNANI AND HOMOEOPATHIC (AYUSH)
DRUGS
Recommendation
3.4 The Committee is of the view that a strong and strict regulatory framework is essential for quality
control of ASU&H drugs. Since the States are responsible for quality control and regulation of AYUSH
drugs, they need financial assistance so as to strengthen their regulatory framework. The Committee notes
that the financial assistance given to States is not much and therefore reiterates its recommendation as given
in 101
st Report for significant enhancement of financial assistance to the States. (Para 3.6)
Action Taken
3.5  The funding pattern to support regulatory and quality control activities of AYUSH drugs in the states
has been enhanced significantly in the National AYUSH Mission (NAM) implemented since November,
2014. In comparison to the erstwhile Central Sponsored Scheme, the funding pattern under the National
AYUSH Mission has been enhanced up to ` 5 crores for state pharmacy, up to ` 4 crores for Drug Testing
Laboratory (DTL), up to ` 50 lakhs for strengthening of regulatory framework, up to ` 25 lakhs per year
for technical manpower of the DTL and up to ` 15 lakhs per year for testing of drug samples.  Nevertheless,
it is for the states to project their requirement of financial assistance in the State Annual Action Plan (SAAP)
of National AYUSH Mission inter-alia for the purpose of quality control of ASU&H drugs and accordingly
the funds are released after necessary approval.
Further Recommendation
3.6 India has a rich heritage of AYUSH systems of medicine, which are widely recognized for
their holistic approach to healthcare.  However, one of the greatest challenges to widespread acceptance
of AYUSH drugs remains quality assurance. Strengthening and modernization of regulatory
framework for quality control of ASU&H drugs is, therefore, a pre-requisite for a strong and effective
system of AYUSH remedies for which it is necessary to step up allocation to State AYUSH drug
regulatory mechanisms.  Though the Committee appreciates the fact that the funding pattern to
support regulatory and quality control activities of the AYUSH drugs in the States has witnessed
improvements since the implementation of National AYUSH Mission in November, 2014, it feels
that a lot more remains to be done to bridge the regulatory gaps.  The Committee would therefore
like the Ministry to sensitize the States to the fact that for equipping AYUSH to achieve tangible
health outcomes, it is imperative that the weakness in the regulatory framework are addressed and
a significant proportion of outlay is projected in their Annual Action Plan for supporting quality
assurance activities.  The Committee desires to be apprised of the initiatives taken by the Ministry
in this regard.
Recommendation
3.7 The Committee would also like to express concern about the issue of failed samples of ASU drugs and
the consequent action taken in this regard. The Committee is of the firm view that merely issuing show cause
notices, departmental action etc. is not enough to control the menace of spurious drugs of AYUSH. Despite
repeated recommendations of the Committee to have stringent measures to tackle the problem of failed
samples, the Ministry seems not to have done anything in this regard. The Committee takes serious note of
the lackadaisical approach of the Ministry in not taking concrete action against defaulters in order to ensure

14
effective regulation of ASU&H drugs. The Committee would like to emphasize that such erring manufacturers
need to be brought to book and dealt with strictly for misleading and duping innocent patients and playing
with their lives. The Committee, accordingly, recommends to the Ministry to lay down stringent regulations
which can act as a deterrent for erring manufacturers. (Para 3.7)
Action Taken
3.8 Misbranded, Adulterated, Spurious and Sub-standard ASU drugs are defined in the Drugs & Cosmetics
Act, 1940 along with the provisions for prohibition of their manufacturing, sale, stocking and distribution;
and the penalty in the form of confiscation of the concerned batch of the drug and payment of fine and/or
imprisonment of the defaulters. As per statute, the power of enforcing these provisions is vested with the
state governments. The states have reported confiscation of such cases of ASU drugs; suspension/ cancellation
of the manufacturing licenses; and prosecution of the defaulters. The Central Government has in the past
banned/ prohibited the manufacturing and sale of ASU products made from tobacco, certain alcoholic
preparations, injections, etc. In order to enforce the ASU drugs related legal provisions in the effective
manner, following steps have been taken:
(i) Ministry of AYUSH has written to the States and supported them for testing of adequate
number of AYUSH drug samples and initiate legal action against the defaulters;
(ii) During 2017-18, the Ministry conducted seven regulatory and quality control training programs
for the ASU&H drug regulators, pharmacy and laboratory staff including manufacturers of all
the states/ UTs;
(iii) An A YUSH vertical has been created in the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization
(CDSCO) w.e.f. 5
th February, 2018 with 12 regulatory posts of Inspectors, Assistant Drugs
Controllers and Deputy Drugs Controllers at the Central level;
(iv) Central sector scheme for safety monitoring of AYUSH drugs and surveillance of the misleading
advertisements has been implemented in 2017-18 to develop an institutional network for detection,
assessment, documenting and reporting of the Adverse Drug Reactions of AYUSH drugs for
appropriate regulatory action;
(v) Financial assistance is being provided through National AYUSH Mission for strengthening the
regulatory and quality control system in the states.
Further Recommendation
3.9 The Committee understands that the power of enforcing the provisions of the Drugs &
Cosmetics Act, 1940 is vested with the State Government.  However, the Central Government is
involved through its schemes and initiatives wherein financial assistance for strengthening the
quality control system through NAM, Central Sector Scheme for safety monitoring of AYUSH
drugs, quality control training programmes in States, creation of a vertical structure in CDSCO
etc is given.  The Committee is of the view that the actual work of the newly created vertical
structure in CDSCO in quality control of drugs and work done for safety monitoring of AYUSH
drugs under the Central Sector Scheme are yet to be seen.  Apart from that, as earlier observed
by the Committee itself, merely issuing directions, show cause notices etc is not sufficient to deal
with the alarming issue at hand.  The Committee has been impressing upon the Ministry to carry
out the required amendment to Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940 so that stringent clauses are included

15
in the Act to effectively deter the erring manufacturers. The Committee however, regrets to
observe that no headway has been made in this regard and desires to be apprised of the hindrances
in this regard. The Committee is aware that the power of enforcing quality control provisions
falls within the purview of State Governments. Nonetheless, given the fact that a part of the plan
outlay of the Ministry is allocated for quality assurance activities, the Committee expects the
Ministry to play a more dynamic role and it is therefore, imperative that certain festering issues
afflicting quality assurance of AYUSH drugs are taken up by the Ministry and corrective measures
suggested thereon.
Recommendation
3.10 Attention of the Committee has been drawn to the fact that last year, 29 Drug laboratories and 46
Pharmacies were available in the public sector in the States and 6 States did not have any manufacturing
unit. The Committee in its 101
st report 2017-18 had recommended that there should be atleast one Drug
Testing Laboratory in each State and more ASU&H drug manufacturing units in the country. The Ministry
in its submission has not given any information about the increase in States Drug Testing Laboratories,
Pharmacies and ASU&H drug manufacturing units. The Committee is constrained to note that the progress
of GMP compliance by manufacturing units across the country has also not been furnished by the Ministry.
The Committee, accordingly, recommends that the Ministry should strive for increasing the number of State
Drug Testing Laboratories for effective regulation of ASU&H drugs and manufacturing units which should
be GMP compliant for producing quality drugs for the people. The Ministry should also furnish the relevant
information to the Committee properly. (Para 3.9)
Action Taken
3.11 During the year 2017-18, seven pharmacies and nine Drug Testing Laboratories in the states have
been provided grant-in-aid through National AYUSH Mission (NAM). In this regard, attention of the Hon’ble
Committee is kindly drawn to the fact that it is the prerogative of State/UT Governments to submit the
proposals for seeking grant-in-aid for establishment or strengthening of pharmacies and laboratories in their
State Annual Action Plans under National AYUSH Mission.
3.12 Besides the availability of Central and State Drug Testing Laboratories, 55 private laboratories are
approved or licensed as of now under the provisions of Drugs& Cosmetic Rules, 1945 and proposals of
more such laboratories are in the pipeline for grant of approval.
3.13 Schedule ‘T’ and Schedule ‘M-I’ under Drugs & Cosmetics Rules, 1945 contain the provisions
of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) for ASU and Homoeopathic drugs respectively. GMP for the
manufacturing of ASU drugs was introduced w.e.f. 7.3.2003 and for Homoeopathic drugs w.e.f.
31.10.2006. As per the available information, 8667 licensed manufacturing units of ASU&H drugs exist
in the country, out of which 7488 (86.7%) units are GMP compliant and 1179 (13.6%) units are
reported not to be complying with GMP norms. Detailed information of State-wise progress about the
number of pharmacies,  GMP compliant units and laboratories for ASU&H drugs from 2015 to current
position is annexed as Annexure-I .
Further Recommendation
3.14 The Committee has been given to understand that there are 88 drug testing laboratories
in the country. The States of Goa, Manipur  and the UTs of Andaman and Nicobar, Dadar &

16
Nagar Haveli, Daman & Diu, Lakshadweep & Puduchery are not having any labs. There were a
total of 9282 Pharmacies in the 36 States/ UTs of the country as on 1 st April, 2015, out of which
7653 were GMP compliant. Presently, there are 8667 Pharmacies, out of which 7488 only are
GMP compliant. The Committee notes that the number of pharmacies has reduced from 9282 to
8667 with maximum reduction in the State of Tamil Nadu.  Apart from that, the number of GMP
compliant units has also declined from 7653 to 7488. The Committee wonders about such decrease
in numbers and the reasons for such a trend is not clear.  The Committee is constrained to note
such decrease in the total number of pharmacies in 2018 compared to 2015. The Committee,
accordingly, would like the Ministry to have an assessment done so as to ascertain the reasons
for the same in consultation with the State Governments especially Tamil Nadu. The Committee
would also like to emphasize that the Ministry needs to make concerted efforts in co-ordination
with State Governments to make these units GMP complaint. Further, States/ UTs where there
are no labs as of now need to be engaged and prompted to contemplate about having atleast one
lab in the State/ UTs.
Recommendation
3.15 With respect to the new legislation containing the existing and proposed provisions of both Drugs and
Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisement) Act, 1954, the Committee
is dismayed to note that the new legislation is still in the process of being framed by the Department of
Health and Family Welfare. It has been more than two years since the new legislation is being framed and
it speaks volumes about the laid back approach of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and also of
the Ministry of AYUSH in pursuing the matter. The Committee would like to strongly recommend that a
definite time line within which this new legislation will see the light of the day may be indicated and the
Ministry of AYUSH should aggressively pursue the matter with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare so
that relevant provisions are incorporated in the legislation and enacted so as to prohibit misleading
advertisements and strengthen the effective regulation of ASU&H drugs. (Para 3.13)
Action Taken
3.16 Drugs & Cosmetics Act,1940 is under the administrative purview of Ministry of Health & Family
Welfare. Accordingly, on the recommendations of the Group of Ministers, the Department of Health &
Family Welfare did take up the task of framing new legislation for Drugs & Cosmetics including Ayurvedic,
Siddha, Unni, Sowa Rigpa and Homoeopathic drugs. For this purpose, Ministry of AYUSH provided
necessary inputs for framing ASU& H drugs related regulatory provisions including stringent penal provisions
for violation of quality norms and standards. The proposed provisions were conceptualized in accordance
with the emerging regulatory trends for effective quality control of ASU&H drugs. The Ministry is pursuing
the matter of imposing effective quality control of ASU&H drugs and introducing prohibitive measures
for misleading advertisements and has inter alia constituted two Empowered Committees chaired by Joint
Secretary level officers vide office order dated 22.3.2018 to monitor the progress of new regulatory
vertical structure of AYUSH in CDSCO and control of misleading advertisement/exaggerated claims
respectively.
Further Recommendation
3.17 The Committee is relieved to know that the Ministry has provided necessary inputs for framing
ASU&H drugs related regulatory provisions for framing a new legislation regarding violation of

17
quality norms and standards.  The Committee, however, is of the view that given the seriousness of
the situation in wake of sale of spurious/ sub-standard ASU drugs, the matter of bringing in a new
legislation in this regard needs to be taken up with the Department of Health and Family Welfare
on a priority basis.  The Committee would also like to be apprised of the composition of the two
Empowered Committees constituted in March, 2018 and the work done by the two Committees with
respect to the regulatory vertical structure of AYUSH for quality assurance and control of misleading
advertisement/ exaggerated claims.
IV. NATIONAL  AYUSH  MISSION
Recommendation
3.18 The Committee appreciates the Ministry of AYUSH for having co-location of AYUSH facilities
at PHCs, CHCs and District Hospitals, participation of AYUSH doctors in National Health Programme
and Public Health Outreach Activities and research activities undertaken to facilitate integration of
Ayurveda and Allopathic system of medicine. The Committee would, however, like to point out that
it is often seen that practitioners of modern system of medicine do not have much faith in AYUSH
system and often question their credibility and scientific validation. The Committee feels that it is a
known fact that our country has been a repository of knowledge of traditional systems of medicine
since ages. The need of the hour is to streamline the AYUSH systems of medicine by standardisation
and quality control of ASU&H drugs and improving the quality of education and healthcare services
through AYUSH. At the same time, the curricula of both modern systems of medicine and AYUSH
system need to be changed in such a way as to strive for integration in the study of medical education
itself followed by cross system referrals and integrated healthcare services. The Committee is of the
view that such an integrated approach towards both systems of medicine would help in understanding
the strengths of each system of medicine and also increase the credibility of AYUSH systems of
medicine. The Committee, accordingly, recommends to the Ministry to take concrete steps in introducing
modules of modern system of medicine in the curriculum and pursue the Ministry of Health and
Family Welfare for introducing similar modules of AYUSH systems of medicines in their MBBS
course. (Para 4.10)
Action Taken
3.19 It may be stated here that the National Policy on Indian Systems of Medicine & Homoeopathy –
2002, envisages integration of AYUSH with the Health Care Delivery System.  Mainstreaming of AYUSH
is one of the strategies in National Health Mission (NHM) as well which seeks to provide accessible,
affordable and quality health care in order to improve the existing health care delivery system.  Government
of India has adopted a strategy of Co-location of AYUSH facilities at Primary Health Centres (PHCs),
Community Health Centres (CHCs) and District Hospitals (DHs), thus enabling choice to the patients for
different systems of medicines under single window.  The engagement of AYUSH Doctors/ paramedics
and their training is supported by the Department of Health & Family Welfare, while the support for
AYUSH infrastructure, equipment/ furniture and medicines are provided by Ministry of AYUSH under
shared responsibilities.
So far as curricula or integrated course and Bridge course is concerned, no such initiatives has been
taken by the Ministry presently.

18
Further Recommendation
3.20 The Committee appreciates the strategy of the National Policy on Indian Systems of Medicine
and Homoeopathy 2002 which envisages integration of AYUSH with health care delivery system
leading to co-location of AYUSH facilities at PHCs, CHCs and District Hospitals. The Committee in
order to bring AYUSH into the mainstream had recommended for change in curriculum which
would include introducing modules of modern medicine in AYUSH system and modules of AYUSH in
the curriculum of modern medicine i.e. MBBS course.  The Committee is of the firm view that the
Ministry of AYUSH needs to take initiative in promoting and integrating Indian systems of medicine
with the modern systems so as to increase its acceptability as a scientific and reliable alternate
system of medicine. The Committee would, however, like to emphasize that the Ministry must lay
focus on increasing the credibility of AYUSH systems by promoting scientific research and upholding
strict quality control of AYUSH drugs.  The Committee, therefore, would like to recommend to the
Ministry to engage with Ministry of Health and Family Welfare for integration of AYUSH systems
with modern medicine.
Recommendation

funds for collaborative research with ICMR for the purposes of standardization and scientific re-validation
of ASU&H drugs. In this way, ASU&H drugs/ remedies will have worldwide acceptance and scientific basis
of AYUSH will be augmented. (Para 5.8)

would include introducing modules of modern medicine in AYUSH system and modules of AYUSH in
the curriculum of modern medicine i.e. MBBS course.  The Committee is of the firm view that the
Ministry of AYUSH needs to take initiative in promoting and integrating Indian systems of medicine
with the modern systems so as to increase its acceptability as a scientific and reliable alternate
system of medicine. The Committee would, however, like to emphasize that the Ministry must lay
focus on increasing the credibility of AYUSH systems by promoting scientific research and upholding
strict quality control of AYUSH drugs.  The Committee, therefore, would like to recommend to the
Ministry to engage with Ministry of Health and Family Welfare for integration of AYUSH systems
with modern medicine. (Para 3.20)

24
The Committee has been given to understand that with respect to CCRH and CCRUM
specifically, the funds allocated to these research institutes were not sufficient and needed to be
enhanced.  The Committee, time and again, has been reiterating on substantial increase in funds
for research in these institutes including collaborative research with ICMR. The Committee would
again like to emphasize that in order to increase the popularity and acceptability of Indian Systems
of Medicine, it is the need of the hour to focus on scientific research including collaborative research
so as to increase the credibility of AYUSH systems by promoting standardization, scientific re-
validation of AYUSH drugs, collaborative research work projects with ICMR etc.  For increasing
such activities which will certainly increase the acceptability of AYUSH, adequate funds need to be
ear-marked for research activities so that the research institutes serve the purpose for which they
have been established. The Committee, therefore, recommends substantial increase to ensure
adequate funds for these research institutes for research purposes. (Para 3.26)
VI. NATIONAL MEDICINAL PLANTS BOARD
The Committee is disappointed to note that there are total 613 UCs pending amounting to
````` 93.65 crore.  There are UCs pending since the years 2001-02 (4 UCs), 2002-03 (18 UCs), 2003-04
(33 UCs) 2004-05 (65 UCs), 2005-06 (76 UCs), 2006-07 (35 UCs), 2007-08 (58 UCs), 2008-09 (44
UCs), 2009-(36 UCs), 2010-11 (39 UCs), 2011-12 (19 UCs), 2012-13 (14 UCs), 2013-14 (21 UCs),
2014-15 (68 UCs) and 2015-16 (83 UCs).  The Committee finds it as an unhealthy trend and has
been reiterating on making efforts for liquidation of UCs.  It also observes that maximum number
of UCs are pending with States like Gujarat ( 35 UCs), Karnataka (36 UCs), Maharashtra (36
UCs), Rajasthan (36 UCs), Tamil Nadu (42 UCs), Uttarakhand (46 UCs), UP (40 UCs) etc. The
Committee, therefore, would like the Ministry to make special efforts for liquidation of pending
UCs of NMPB as the very objective of the scheme would be defeated and conservation, development
and sustainable management of medicinal plants would be hamstrung if pendency is not liquidated.
(Para 3.30)

PREFACE 
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and 
Family Welfare, having been authorized by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, 
present this One Hundred Fifteenth Report of the Committee on the National Commission for 
Indian System of Medicine Bill, 2019. 
2. In  pursuance of Rule 270 of the Rules  of Procedure and Conduct of  Business in the 
Council of States relating  to the Department -related Parliamentary Standing  Committees, the 
Chairman, Rajya Sabha, referred* the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine Bill, 
2019 (Annexure I) on the 14th  January, 201 9 as introduced  in the Rajya Sabha on the 7th 
January, 2019 for examination and report  by  30th January, 2 019. However, the previous 
Committee could not consider the Bill and present its Report and requested for extension of time.  
Subsequently, Hon'ble Chairman , Rajya Sabha  granted exten sion of time for presentation of 
Report on the Bill upto 29th April, 2019.  However, the deliberations on the said Bill could not be 
concluded due to preoccupation of the Members of the previous Committee in the General 
Elections for the 17th Lok Sabha and subsequent dissolution of the Committee.   
3. The previous Committee  started the e xamination of the Bill and held 24th January, 2019 
sitting where it heard the views of Secretary, Ministry of AYUSH on the Bill . The Committee 
also issued a Press Release inviting memoranda/views from individuals and other stakeholders. 
In response thereto, a number of memoranda from different organization/association and 
individuals were received.  
4.  The re-constituted Committee held 4 sittings during the course of examination of the Bill, 
i.e., on 21st, 22 nd October, 7th and 15 th November 2019. The list of witnesses heard by the 
Committee is at Annexure-II. 
5. The Committee considered the draft Report and adopted the same on 15th November, 
2019. 
6. The Committee relied on the following documents in finalizing its Report:- 
(i) The National Commission for Indian System of Medicine Bill, 2019; 
(ii) Background Note on the Bill received from the Ministry of AYUSH; 
(iii) Presentation, clarifications and Oral evidence of Secretary, Ministry of AYUSH; 
(iv) Memoranda received on the Bill from various 
institutes/bodies/associations/organizations/experts and replies of the Ministry on 
the memoranda selected by the Committee for examination; 
__________________________________(iii)_________________________________________ 

 
 
* Rajya Sabha Parliamentary Bulletin Part II, No.58476, dated 14 th  January, 2019. 
 
 
(v) Oral evidence and written submissions by various stakeholders/experts on the 
Bill; and 
(vi) Replies received from the Ministry of AYUSH  to the questions/queries  raised by 
Members during the meetings on the Bill 
7. On behalf of the Committee, I would like to acknowledge with thanks the contributions made 
by those who deposed before the Committee and also those who gave their valuable suggestions 
to the Committee through their written submissions.
